lessons.title: Converting Units
sourceActivityPurposes: Mental fraction-of-whole warm-up with connected halves, quarters and eighths
Cross-system conversion for a road speed sign with approximation and unit-direction reasoning
Animal mass conversions with paired pounds and kilograms and a stated weight threshold, not medical advice
Kitchen volume conversions from cups to tablespoons and back with fractional measures
requiredRepresentations: ratio table with BOTH quantity units
accessible double number line aligned in cups/tablespoons
text description of foreign metric speed-limit sign without reproducing the original image
grade6OriginalTeachingAdded: Worked unit-rate speed comparison in BOTH directions: 75 mph ≈ 120 km/h, 80 km/h ≈ 50 mph
Worked model mass table for 88, 33, 5.5 and 55 pounds at 2.2 lb/kg
Worked cup/tablespoon mixed-number and decimal conversions with original accessible text table

criteria: Use a correctly labeled conversion equality and justify multiplier direction
Compute with equivalent ratios and correct reciprocal conversions
Show at least one accurate table/number-line relation with units
Distinguish classroom weight conversion from actual animal medication decisions

caveats: Sign and original photograph not reproduced
Approximate 8 km : 5 miles is not exact SI conversion.

lessons.title: Comparing Speeds and Prices
sourceActivityPurposes: Estimate quotient relative to half, one or one-and-a-half
Compare three treadmill workouts using mixed metric distance and time units, including an extended lead-time question
Compare posted offers for matching-size cans and an optional different-size can at per-ounce price
Explain what a 'best deal' may mean beyond a numerical sticker price
requiredRepresentations: meters/minute comparison table for three runners
price per can table for equal-size products
price per ounce comparison for different can sizes with explicit denominator
grade6OriginalTeachingAdded: Source treadmill numerical rates 140, 210, 140 m/min and a 1-km catch-up/lead model
First-party per-item and per-ounce store tables; equal $0.05 per ounce for two options
Explicit teacher boundary for nonnumeric shopping reasons

criteria: Convert hours and kilometers before comparing
Justify equal unit rates despite different totals
Normalize per item versus per ounce correctly
Support the response with a shopping context if the task asks for personal best deal

caveats: A 1-km lead calculation depends on same time, direction and constant speeds.

lessons.title: Interpreting Rates
sourceActivityPurposes: Collect verbally familiar 'per' examples from group discussion
Use water/oats cooking model to justify both rate directions
Compute two unit rates for food, milk consumption, and ticket pricing, then select the useful rate
Draft/critique an advertising offer, an open reasoning task with no unique numeric grading
requiredRepresentations: two-column table in water-cups and oats-cups with distinct rate-per-one rows
spoken and written rate comparison with quantity units
grade6OriginalTeachingAdded: First-party reciprocal oatmeal rates 2.5 water/oat and 0.4 oat/water
Applied reciprocal rates for 35 ounces sugar, 3 gallons milk, and 1,000 raffle tickets
Explicit teacher-scoring boundary for nonnumeric persuasion

criteria: Identify the two reciprocal rates with different compound units
Choose and justify the correct orientation for the unknown
Explain why different reciprocal numbers describe the same ratio
Evaluate advertising claims with human reviewed comparison and stated assumption

caveats: Class group-list quality and persuasive advertising cannot be certified by a numeric-only checker.

lessons.title: Equivalent Ratios Have the Same Unit Rates
sourceActivityPurposes: Open warm-up about unlike-looking speed descriptions with multiple defensible explanations
Demonstrate constant burrito unit price across a table, including a symbolic doubling argument
Complete bracelet production and reverse elapsed-time table using constant per-hour rate
Complete pounds-of-apples to cups-of-applesauce two-way ratio table
Explore simultaneous eating and water-flow problems under explicit fixed-rate assumptions
requiredRepresentations: accessible ratio tables with quantity and rate columns
column-to-column rate operator and row-to-row scale-factor comparison
written algebra c/b = 2c/2b for positive b
open discussion outcomes not forced to one selection
grade6OriginalTeachingAdded: Burrito price, bracelet counts and applesauce yield examples with independent inverse reasoning
Optional 200-minute 750-gallon two-hose model with explicit constant-flow caveat
Teacher-review boundary for open choice of which rate differs

criteria: Keep unit rate invariant across all positive scaled rows
Compute forward and inverse quantities with correct units
Explain symbolically why both values scaled by the same positive factor keep the quotient
Accept mathematically justified alternatives in an open comparison task

caveats: 16.6667 hours displayed as a rounding only; exact duration is 50/3 hours.
